correctness.rationale: The three limits follow from the exact decomposition of the generalized matching count into the known-correct count and the fixed-point count of the residual uniform permutation. In the sparse-skill endpoint, the known-correct count converges in total variation to a Poisson law, the residual size diverges in probability, and the conditional fixed-point law converges in total variation to Pois(1); addition gives the stated Poisson limit. In the near-perfect endpoint, the unresolved count converges in total variation to a Poisson law and the moved-point kernel gives the explicit derangement mixture. In the interior, the binomial variance diverges, while the residual fixed-point count is tight with expectation at most one; Slutsky's theorem gives the stated centered normal limit. Exact finite checks passed but are not used as the universal proof.

The explicit near-perfect mismatch law is useful because it is non-Gaussian and rules out exactly one mismatch; this supplies a concrete boundary distribution where the source literature notes standard asymptotic inference can be unreliable.
